title: Practice 8: Perfective or imperfective? The prefixed verbs in use

blocks.text: Exercises: sentences from Tatoeba (tatoeba.org, CC BY 2.0 FR) and from the library's public-domain books.

exercises.q: Tom took Mary to Acapulco.
exercises.why: **свозил** is the past tense (masculine) of **свозить** ((transitive) to transport down, to drive down; to transport away, to carry away (by vehicle)) — imperfective; its perfective partner is **свезти**. past: он свози́л · она свози́ла · оно свози́ло · они свози́ли. — Wiktionary, «свозить» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «Any prefix (except "по-"), added to the imperf. pair of "going verbs" (to both, repeated and actual functions), makes them an ordinary imperfective-perfective pair.» — DLI, Lesson 56.  «The unidirectional verb serves as the base for the perfective, and the multidirectional as the base for the imperfective.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «**с-, со-** — Movement downwards. Antonym: вз- Example: После представления актёр сошёл со сцены. — After the performance, the actor got off the stage. Prepositional phrases: с + gen.; на + acc.; к + dat.; за + inst.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  The other choice: **свёз** is perfective (**свезти**).  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).
exercises.context: Motion verbs combine with prefixes to form new aspectual pairs, which lose the distinction of directionality, but gain spatial or temporal meanings. (Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0))

exercises.q: I spent a week in the hospital.
exercises.why: **провёл** is the past tense (masculine) of **провести** (to lead, to conduct, to guide, to steer, to take; to lay, to construct, to build, to install a road, a pipe, a wire etc.) — perfective; its imperfective partner is **проводить**. past: он провёл · она провела́ · оно провело́ · они провели́. — Wiktionary, «провести» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «Any prefix (except "по-"), added to the imperf. pair of "going verbs" (to both, repeated and actual functions), makes them an ordinary imperfective-perfective pair.» — DLI, Lesson 56.  «The unidirectional verb serves as the base for the perfective, and the multidirectional as the base for the imperfective.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «**про-** — Movement across, through, or past something Example: Мы проехали через город. — We drove through the city. Мы прошли мимо станции метро. — We passed the metro station. Prepositional phrases: сквозь / через / в + acc.; мимо + gen.; without preposition.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  Compare: «Я хорошо провёл время.» (I had a good time.) — DLI, Lesson 79. «Мы провели в Европе два месяца.» (We spent two months in Europe.) — DLI, Lesson 79.  The other choice: **проводил** is imperfective (**проводить**).  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).
exercises.context: Motion verbs combine with prefixes to form new aspectual pairs, which lose the distinction of directionality, but gain spatial or temporal meanings. (Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0))

exercises.q: They came in full force.
exercises.why: **пришли** is the past tense (plural) of **прийти** (to come (to), to arrive (at)) — perfective; its imperfective partner is **приходить**. past: он пришёл · она пришла́ · оно пришло́ · они пришли́. — Wiktionary, «прийти» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «Any prefix (except "по-"), added to the imperf. pair of "going verbs" (to both, repeated and actual functions), makes them an ordinary imperfective-perfective pair.» — DLI, Lesson 56.  «The unidirectional verb serves as the base for the perfective, and the multidirectional as the base for the imperfective.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «**при-** — Intended arrival, signals presence of the agent at a location as a result of motion. Antonym: у- Example: Он приехал в Москву неделю назад. — He arrived in Moscow a week ago. Prepositional phrases: в / на + acc.; к + dat.; из / с / от + gen.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «Note. — The verbs приходить and приезжать usually refer to the habitual or repeated actions: Он приходит (приезжает) сюда каждый день. — He comes here every day. These verbs, as the other verbs of motion, may be used to express a single action in the future: Он приходит на работу завтра утром. — He is coming to work tomorrow morning. Она приезжает из Москвы сегодня вечером. — She is coming (arriving) from Moscow this evening. When the action is in progress in the present such expressions as "He is coming" or "He is on the way here" are expressed in Russian in the following way: Кто это идёт (едет) сюда?» — DLI, Lesson 24.  Compare: «Приходите сюда завтра!» (Come here tomorrow!) — DLI, Lesson 24.  The other choice: **приходили** is imperfective (**приходить**).  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).
exercises.context: Motion verbs combine with prefixes to form new aspectual pairs, which lose the distinction of directionality, but gain spatial or temporal meanings. (Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0))

exercises.q: Have you ever got across a river by swimming?
exercises.why: **переплывал** is the past tense (masculine) of **переплывать** (to swim across; to sail across) — imperfective; its perfective partner is **переплыть**. past: он переплыва́л · она переплыва́ла · оно переплыва́ло · они переплыва́ли. — Wiktionary, «переплывать» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «Any prefix (except "по-"), added to the imperf. pair of "going verbs" (to both, repeated and actual functions), makes them an ordinary imperfective-perfective pair.» — DLI, Lesson 56.  «The unidirectional verb serves as the base for the perfective, and the multidirectional as the base for the imperfective.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «**пере-** — Movement across, from one point to another; through Example: Утки переплыли реку. — The ducks swam across the river. Prepositional phrases: через + acc.; without preposition + acc.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  The other choice: **переплыл** is perfective (**переплыть**).  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).
exercises.context: Motion verbs combine with prefixes to form new aspectual pairs, which lose the distinction of directionality, but gain spatial or temporal meanings. (Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0))

exercises.q: Tom leveled a shotgun at me.
exercises.why: **навёл** is the past tense (masculine) of **навести** (to direct (at), to aim (at), to point (at); to cover, to coat, to apply) — perfective; its imperfective partner is **наводить**. past: он навёл · она навела́ · оно навело́ · они навели́. — Wiktionary, «навести» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «Any prefix (except "по-"), added to the imperf. pair of "going verbs" (to both, repeated and actual functions), makes them an ordinary imperfective-perfective pair.» — DLI, Lesson 56.  «The unidirectional verb serves as the base for the perfective, and the multidirectional as the base for the imperfective.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «**на-** — Movement onto the surface of an object; only formed from multidirectional verb of motion Example: Туча наползла на солнце. — A cloud crept onto the sun. Prepositional phrases: в/на + acc.; without preposition + acc.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  The other choice: **наводил** is imperfective (**наводить**).  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).
exercises.context: Motion verbs combine with prefixes to form new aspectual pairs, which lose the distinction of directionality, but gain spatial or temporal meanings. (Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0))

exercises.q: The economy has entered a recession.
exercises.why: **вошла** is the past tense (feminine) of **войти** (to enter, to go in(to) (by foot), to get in(to); to penetrate into) — perfective; its imperfective partner is **входить**. past: он вошёл · она вошла́ · оно вошло́ · они вошли́. — Wiktionary, «войти» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «Any prefix (except "по-"), added to the imperf. pair of "going verbs" (to both, repeated and actual functions), makes them an ordinary imperfective-perfective pair.» — DLI, Lesson 56.  «The unidirectional verb serves as the base for the perfective, and the multidirectional as the base for the imperfective.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «**в-, во-** — Movement inwards across a threshold, entering. Antonym: вы- Example: Трамвай остановился, и девушка вошла. — The tram stopped and the girl entered. Prepositional phrases: в / на + acc.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  Compare: «Я вошёл в комнату и открыл окно.» (Perfective) — DLI, Lesson 56. «Я войду в комнату и открою окно.» — DLI, Lesson 56.  The other choice: **входила** is imperfective (**входить**).  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).
exercises.context: Motion verbs combine with prefixes to form new aspectual pairs, which lose the distinction of directionality, but gain spatial or temporal meanings. (Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0))

exercises.q: He dropped in to see us.
exercises.why: **зашёл** is the past tense (masculine) of **зайти** (to go (to see), to come in (to see, etc.), to call, to drop in; to pick up, to fetch) — perfective; its imperfective partner is **заходить**. past: он зашёл · она зашла́ · оно зашло́ · они зашли́. — Wiktionary, «зайти» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «Any prefix (except "по-"), added to the imperf. pair of "going verbs" (to both, repeated and actual functions), makes them an ordinary imperfective-perfective pair.» — DLI, Lesson 56.  «The unidirectional verb serves as the base for the perfective, and the multidirectional as the base for the imperfective.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «**за-** — Movement behind an object; stopping off on the way Example: Старушка зашла за угол и исчезла. — The old woman walked behind the corner and disappeared. Prepositional phrases: в / на / за + acc.; к + dat.; за + inst.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  The other choice: **заходил** is imperfective (**заходить**).  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).
exercises.context: Motion verbs combine with prefixes to form new aspectual pairs, which lose the distinction of directionality, but gain spatial or temporal meanings. (Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0))

exercises.q: The story drew to a conclusion.
exercises.why: **подошла** is the past tense (feminine) of **подойти** (to approach, to come to, to walk to, to draw near [with к (k)]; to fit, to suit, to match, to be right [with dative]) — perfective; its imperfective partner is **подходить**. past: он подошёл · она подошла́ · оно подошло́ · они подошли́. — Wiktionary, «подойти» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «Any prefix (except "по-"), added to the imperf. pair of "going verbs" (to both, repeated and actual functions), makes them an ordinary imperfective-perfective pair.» — DLI, Lesson 56.  «The unidirectional verb serves as the base for the perfective, and the multidirectional as the base for the imperfective.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «**под-, подо-** — Approach. Antonym: от- Example: Он подошёл к девушке, чтобы спросить её номер. — He approached the girl to ask for her number. Prepositional phrases: к + dat.; до + gen.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  The other choice: **подходила** is imperfective (**подходить**).  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).

exercises.q: I crawled out of bed and got dressed.
exercises.why: **выполз** is the past tense (masculine) of **выползти** (to creep out, to crawl out; (colloquial) to drag oneself out) — perfective; its imperfective partner is **выползать**. past: он вы́полз · она вы́ползла · оно вы́ползло · они вы́ползли. — Wiktionary, «выползти» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «Any prefix (except "по-"), added to the imperf. pair of "going verbs" (to both, repeated and actual functions), makes them an ordinary imperfective-perfective pair.» — DLI, Lesson 56.  «The unidirectional verb serves as the base for the perfective, and the multidirectional as the base for the imperfective.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «**вы-** — Movement out of something across a threshold, exiting. Antonym: в- Example: Она вышла из кабинета. — She exited the office. Prepositional phrases: из / с / от + gen.; в / на + acc.; к + dat.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  The other choice: **выползал** is imperfective (**выползать**).  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).

exercises.q: I saw Tom swimming across the river.
exercises.why: **переплывал** is the past tense (masculine) of **переплывать** (to swim across; to sail across) — imperfective; its perfective partner is **переплыть**. past: он переплыва́л · она переплыва́ла · оно переплыва́ло · они переплыва́ли. — Wiktionary, «переплывать» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «Any prefix (except "по-"), added to the imperf. pair of "going verbs" (to both, repeated and actual functions), makes them an ordinary imperfective-perfective pair.» — DLI, Lesson 56.  «The unidirectional verb serves as the base for the perfective, and the multidirectional as the base for the imperfective.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «**пере-** — Movement across, from one point to another; through Example: Утки переплыли реку. — The ducks swam across the river. Prepositional phrases: через + acc.; without preposition + acc.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  The other choice: **переплыл** is perfective (**переплыть**).  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).
exercises.context: Motion verbs combine with prefixes to form new aspectual pairs, which lose the distinction of directionality, but gain spatial or temporal meanings. (Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0))

exercises.q: Tom let the garden go to rack and ruin.
exercises.why: **довёл** is the past tense (masculine) of **довести** (to lead, to take, to accompany (to), to bring (into); (cooking) to scald) — perfective; its imperfective partner is **доводить**. past: он довёл · она довела́ · оно довело́ · они довели́. — Wiktionary, «довести» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «Any prefix (except "по-"), added to the imperf. pair of "going verbs" (to both, repeated and actual functions), makes them an ordinary imperfective-perfective pair.» — DLI, Lesson 56.  «The unidirectional verb serves as the base for the perfective, and the multidirectional as the base for the imperfective.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «**до-** — Reaching a limit or destination Example: Пассажиры доехали до последней остановки и вышли из автобуса. — The passengers reached the last station and exited the bus. Prepositional phrases: до + gen.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  The other choice: **доводил** is imperfective (**доводить**).  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).
exercises.context: Motion verbs combine with prefixes to form new aspectual pairs, which lose the distinction of directionality, but gain spatial or temporal meanings. (Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0))

exercises.q: The birds flew away in all directions.
exercises.why: **разлетелись** is the past tense (plural) of **разлететься** (to fly away, to scatter (in the air); to come apart, to be blown apart) — perfective; its imperfective partner is **разлетаться**. past: он разлете́лся · она разлете́лась · оно разлете́лось · они разлете́лись. — Wiktionary, «разлететься» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «Any prefix (except "по-"), added to the imperf. pair of "going verbs" (to both, repeated and actual functions), makes them an ordinary imperfective-perfective pair.» — DLI, Lesson 56.  «The unidirectional verb serves as the base for the perfective, and the multidirectional as the base for the imperfective.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «**раз-, разо-, рас- (+сь, +ся)** — Divergent movement in various directions from one center. Antonym: с-, со- (+сь, +ся) Example: Дед Мороз разнёс подарки по домам. — Grandfather Frost brought the gifts to the (various) houses. После ужина, мы разошлись по домам. — After dinner, we went to our separate homes. Prepositional phrases: по + dat. pl.; в + acc. pl.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  The other choice: **разлетались** is imperfective (**разлетаться**).  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).
exercises.context: Motion verbs combine with prefixes to form new aspectual pairs, which lose the distinction of directionality, but gain spatial or temporal meanings. (Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0))

exercises.q: Tom took his children to a pet store.
exercises.why: **сводил** is the past tense (masculine) of **сводить** (to lead, to take (from somewhere); to bring together, to throw together) — imperfective; its perfective partner is **свести**. past: он своди́л · она своди́ла · оно своди́ло · они своди́ли. — Wiktionary, «сводить» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «Any prefix (except "по-"), added to the imperf. pair of "going verbs" (to both, repeated and actual functions), makes them an ordinary imperfective-perfective pair.» — DLI, Lesson 56.  «The unidirectional verb serves as the base for the perfective, and the multidirectional as the base for the imperfective.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «**с-, со-** — Movement downwards. Antonym: вз- Example: После представления актёр сошёл со сцены. — After the performance, the actor got off the stage. Prepositional phrases: с + gen.; на + acc.; к + dat.; за + inst.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  The other choice: **свёл** is perfective (**свести**).  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).
